images.filename: Bristol Harbour (St Stephen's Church, St Augustine the Less Church, Bristol Cathedral), BRO Picbox-7-PBA-22, 1250x1250.jpg
images.caption: Black and white etching of the harbour in Bristol, England in about 1850, with 10 sailing vessels and rowing boats. The towers in the background are those of St Stephen's parish church (left), St Augustine the Less (centre) and Bristol Cathedral (right). The channel was filled in 1892–1938 and the church of St Augustine the Less was demolished in 1962.
images.alt: Black and white etching of the harbour in Bristol, England in about 1850, with 10 sailing vessels and rowing boats. The towers in the background are those of St Stephen's parish church (left), St Augustine the Less (centre) and Bristol Cathedral (right). The channel was filled in 1892–1938 and the church of St Augustine the Less was demolished in 1962.
images.artist: Unknown, published c.1850. Image from the collections of Bristol Record Office

images.caption:
Bristol Parkway railway station, GloucestershireOpened in 1972 by British Rail where its lines from Birmingham to Bristol and London to South Wales cross.
View west towards Bristol and South Wales from the east-bound platform. When opened there were only 2 platform faces, a modest car park and a small booking hall. By 2021 the car park was double decked (far right), a larger booking hall had been opened (centre right), there were 4 platform faces and the railway line had been electrified.
images.alt:
Bristol Parkway railway station, GloucestershireOpened in 1972 by British Rail where its lines from Birmingham to Bristol and London to South Wales cross.
View west towards Bristol and South Wales from the east-bound platform. When opened there were only 2 platform faces, a modest car park and a small booking hall.
